sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日简报《DealBook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的DealBook峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的领导人，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zilran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及其他许多人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 届时，您可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at NYTimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 我们将在11月18日于NYTimes.com上直播部分采访内容，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果您还不是订阅用户，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻内容的一个月免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望您能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 您一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: Today, in the closely watched Georgia runoffs, the Democrats win one race and are heavily favored in the second, putting Democratic control of the Senate within reach.
sentences.zh: 今天，在备受关注的佐治亚州决选中，民主党人赢下了一场竞选，并在第二场中占据明显优势，这使得民主党控制参议院的目标触手可及。

sentences.en: My colleague, Nate Cohn, on a historic night in Georgia.
sentences.zh: 我的同事内特·科恩将带我们回顾佐治亚州这个历史性的夜晚。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, January 6th.
sentences.zh: 今天是1月6日，星期三。

sentences.en: Well, Nate, good morning.
sentences.zh: 内特，早上好。

sentences.en: Good morning.
sentences.zh: 早上好。

sentences.en: I have to say, this was not a telephone call or an election call that we were expecting to have tonight.
sentences.zh: 我不得不说，今晚的选举结果和我们预期的不太一样。

sentences.en: You know, I'm surprised to hear that.
sentences.zh: 你知道，听到这个我很惊讶。

sentences.en: Does that mean there was worse planning on your end than I typically expect from you guys?
sentences.zh: 这是否意味着你们那边的计划比我通常预期的要糟糕？

sentences.en: I mean, we had it on really good journalistic authority that the Georgia Senate runoffs were going to take days to count.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们从非常可靠的新闻来源得知，佐治亚州参议院决选的计票工作需要几天时间。

sentences.en: And here we are, I guess, seven hours after the polls close, and we have real news from this race.
sentences.zh: 而现在，我想是在投票站关闭七小时后，我们已经有了这场竞选的真实消息。

sentences.en: It's true.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: We have a projection.
sentences.zh: 我们已经有了预测结果。

sentences.en: So, Nate, tell us exactly where things stand at 2.30 a.m.
sentences.zh: 那么，内特，请告诉我们凌晨2点半时，

sentences.en: on Wednesday morning in these runoffs.
sentences.zh: 这些决选的局势究竟如何。

sentences.en: Well, there are two contests, and one of them we have a projected winner.
sentences.zh: 目前有两场竞选，其中一场我们已经预测了获胜者。

sentences.en: The Democrat, Raphael Warnock, has defeated Kelly Loeffler in the Senate special election.
sentences.zh: 民主党人拉斐尔·沃诺克在参议院特别选举中击败了凯利·洛夫勒。

sentences.en: And in the regular Senate election between John Ossoff and David Perdue,
sentences.zh: 而在乔恩·奥索夫和大卫·珀杜之间的常规参议院选举中，

sentences.en: the Democrat, John Ossoff, has a slight lead of a few thousand votes with nearly all of the vote in and counted.
sentences.zh: 民主党人乔恩·奥索夫以几千票的微弱优势领先，目前几乎所有选票都已统计完毕。

sentences.en: So, help us understand how we can have one Senate race called, the other not called.
sentences.zh: 那么，请帮我们理解为什么一场参议院竞选有了结果，而另一场却没有。

sentences.en: Because I'm having a little bit of trouble imagining in a race where two Democrats are on the ballot
sentences.zh: 因为我有点难以想象，在两名民主党人和两名共和党人同时出现在选票上的竞选中，

sentences.en: and two Republicans are on the ballot, understanding how one Democratic Senate candidate gets ahead of the other.
sentences.zh: 为什么一位民主党参议院候选人会领先于另一位。

sentences.en: I had long imagined that any Democratic voter who cast a ballot was going to cast a ballot for both.
sentences.zh: 我一直以为任何投下选票的民主党选民都会为两人都投票。

sentences.en: That's certainly a reasonable expectation.
sentences.zh: 这确实是一个合理的预期。

sentences.en: You know, I think that there are a lot of people who vote based on personality, based on how much they like somebody.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我认为很多人是基于个人魅力，基于他们对某人的喜爱程度来投票的。

sentences.en: And as far back as the November election, it was clear that the Democrats were better positioned in the special election than they were in the regularly scheduled election.
sentences.zh: 早在11月的选举中，就很明显民主党在特别选举中的处境要比在常规选举中好。

sentences.en: I think there are a couple of explanations.
sentences.zh: 我认为有几个解释。

sentences.en: One is that the Republicans had a pretty brutal primary in the run-up to the November special election.
sentences.zh: 首先，共和党在11月特别选举前的初选中经历了一场相当残酷的竞争。

sentences.en: And Kelly Loeffler ran pretty far to the right in that primary.
sentences.zh: 凯利·洛夫勒在那次初选中立场非常右倾。

sentences.en: You may recall that she ran a television advertisement claiming that she was further to the right than Attila the Hun.
sentences.zh: 你可能还记得，她曾播放过一个电视广告，声称自己的立场比匈奴王阿提拉还要右。

sentences.en: In contrast, there was not a fierce inter-party battle on the right for the regularly scheduled election.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，在常规选举中，右翼内部并没有激烈的党内斗争。

sentences.en: David Perdue was a well-established incumbent and who, despite being very conservative,
sentences.zh: 大卫·珀杜是一位根基稳固的现任议员，尽管他非常保守，

sentences.en: still has a little bit of appeal to a traditionally Republican voter that maybe has swung over to the Democrats in recent cycles.
sentences.zh: 但他对那些在最近几轮选举中可能转向民主党的传统共和党选民仍有一点吸引力。

sentences.en: And we're talking about a very small number of voters, to be clear at the moment.
sentences.zh: 需要明确的是，我们现在谈论的是极少数选民。

sentences.en: There's only about a percentage point that separates the two candidates.
sentences.zh: 两位候选人之间的差距仅为一个百分点左右。

sentences.en: So it doesn't take much to create this sort of seemingly significant difference.
sentences.zh: 所以，一点点变动就足以造成这种看似重大的差异。

sentences.en: Well, what is the fact that the race has been called for Raphael Warnock but not for John Ossoff?
sentences.zh: 那么，拉斐尔·沃诺克的竞选结果已经出炉，而乔恩·奥索夫的还没有，这说明了什么？

sentences.en: Tell us about exactly who showed up for this election.
sentences.zh: 请告诉我们到底是谁参加了这次选举。

sentences.en: I don't think it tells us anything.
sentences.zh: 我不认为这说明了什么。

sentences.en: I think that basically under any plausible turnout scenario, we expected Warnock to be in the stronger position in this race.
sentences.zh: 我认为在任何合理的投票率情况下，我们都预计沃诺克在这场竞选中会处于更有利的地位。

sentences.en: That wasn't inevitable, of course, but that was the expectation.
sentences.zh: 当然，这并非必然，但这是预期之中的。

sentences.en: We do know from the results that we see at the precinct level and by county that the Democrats enjoyed a really strong turnout in this election.
sentences.zh: 我们从选区和县级的结果中确实看到，民主党人在这次选举中享受了非常高的投票率。

sentences.en: A higher proportion of voters appeared to return to the polls for this runoff election in Democratic-leaning precincts and counties,
sentences.zh: 在倾向民主党的选区和县，回到投票站参加这次决选的选民比例更高，

sentences.en: and in particular in majority black precincts and counties, than did in counties that voted for the president or were majority whites without a degree.
sentences.zh: 特别是在黑人占多数的选区和县，比那些投票给总统或白人占多数且没有大学学历的县要高。

sentences.en: That feels significant.
sentences.zh: 这感觉意义重大。

sentences.en: We do not understand special elections, runoff elections, to ever draw the same kind of turnout that presidential elections draw.
sentences.zh: 我们并不认为特别选举或决选会像总统大选那样吸引同样的投票率。

sentences.en: So this feels very unique.
sentences.zh: 所以这感觉非常独特。

sentences.en: Yeah, this is a huge turnout.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个巨大的投票率。

sentences.en: I mean there were a lot of truly terrible turnout predictions over the last two months.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，过去两个月里有很多关于投票率的糟糕预测。

sentences.en: And at the moment I think the turnout is close to 90 percent of the general election.
sentences.zh: 目前我认为投票率接近大选的90%。

sentences.en: More people voted in this election than voted in Georgia in the 2016 presidential election.
sentences.zh: 这次选举的投票人数超过了2016年佐治亚州总统大选的投票人数。

sentences.en: Now, granted, there's been population growth in Georgia since then, and Georgia has become a more competitive state at the presidential level since then,
sentences.zh: 当然，自那时以来佐治亚州的人口有所增长，而且佐治亚州在总统层面的竞争也变得更加激烈，

sentences.en: and this was a brace for control of the Senate.
sentences.zh: 再加上这是一场争夺参议院控制权的竞选。

sentences.en: But I think that indicates that this was – I mean this was basically a presidential electorate that we had
sentences.zh: 但我认为这表明——我的意思是，这基本上是一场总统级别的选民参与，

sentences.en: when typically a runoff election might be expected to look like at best a midterm but often even a lower turnout election than that,
sentences.zh: 而通常情况下，决选的投票率充其量可能被预期为中期选举水平，甚至更低，

sentences.en: something more like a primary election than a midterm election.
sentences.zh: 更像是初选而不是中期选举。

sentences.en: Now, you started to mention the turnout of black voters in Georgia, and I wonder how significant that was
sentences.zh: 现在，你开始提到佐治亚州黑人选民的投票率，我想知道这有多重要，

sentences.en: and how central you think that is to Warnock's projected victory and Ossoff's lead so far.
sentences.zh: 以及你认为这对沃诺克的预测胜利和奥索夫目前的领先地位有多核心。

sentences.en: It's a huge part of it.
sentences.zh: 这是其中非常重要的一部分。

sentences.en: Georgia has the second or third largest black population in the country.
sentences.zh: 佐治亚州拥有全国第二或第三大黑人人口。

sentences.en: In the general election, it was probably something just short of 30 percent of the vote, and so that's a majority of the Democratic voters in this state.
sentences.zh: 在大选中，这部分选票可能占了不到30%，所以这是该州民主党选民的多数。

sentences.en: All indications that we have right now suggest that the black share of the electorate was higher in these runoff elections than it was in the general election in November.
sentences.zh: 我们目前所有的迹象都表明，黑人在这次决选中的选民份额高于11月的大选。

sentences.en: It's still too early to pin that down with precision.
sentences.zh: 现在要精确确定这一点还为时过早。

sentences.en: We'll get authoritative data on that in the weeks ahead, but all the data that we have at this point suggests that the increase in black turnout
sentences.zh: 我们将在未来几周内获得权威数据，但目前我们掌握的所有数据都表明，黑人投票率的下降，

sentences.en: or maybe put more precisely the decrease in black turnout compared to the general election
sentences.zh: 或者更准确地说，与大选相比黑人投票率的下降，

sentences.en: was smaller than the decrease in white turnout or Latino turnout or particularly white working class turnout.
sentences.zh: 要小于白人投票率、拉丁裔投票率，尤其是白人工人阶级投票率的下降。

sentences.en: So all the mobilization that we have been hearing about and talking about on the daily of the black Georgia electorate for this runoff,
sentences.zh: 所以，我们一直在《每日新闻》中听到和谈论的关于佐治亚州黑人选民为这次决选进行的动员，

sentences.en: and really I guess starting with the presidential election, that has truly potentially made the difference here in at least one and possibly both of these Senate runoffs.
sentences.zh: 实际上我想是从总统大选开始的，这确实可能在至少一场、甚至两场参议院决选中起到了决定性作用。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that that extra mobilization, that relative increase in the black share of the electorate
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为那种额外的动员，即黑人选民份额的相对增加，

sentences.en: could easily prove to be the decisive factor in Democrats taking back the Senate when we have all the data in to say for sure.
sentences.zh: 当我们掌握所有数据后，很可能被证明是民主党夺回参议院的决定性因素。

sentences.en: So based on the current vote counting, should we assume that John Ossoff stands a reasonably good chance of pulling out a victory of his own like Warnock?
sentences.zh: 那么根据目前的计票结果，我们是否应该假设乔恩·奥索夫像沃诺克一样，有相当大的机会取得胜利？

sentences.en: I mean, just how connected are these two races?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这两场竞选之间的联系有多紧密？

sentences.en: Is it possible to imagine that the Democrats win one seat, the Warnock seat, and the Republicans win the other seat, the Perdue seat?
sentences.zh: 是否可以想象民主党赢下一个席位（沃诺克的席位），而共和党赢下另一个席位（珀杜的席位）？

sentences.en: I don't think that's realistic at this point.
sentences.zh: 我不认为这在目前是现实的。

sentences.en: There's not going to be a call for a little bit.
sentences.zh: 短时间内不会有最终结果。

sentences.en: If you remember from the general election, the news organizations are reluctant to call these races until a candidate leads by more than the margin of a recount.
sentences.zh: 如果你还记得大选的情况，新闻机构在候选人领先优势超过重新计票的门槛之前，是不愿宣布竞选结果的。

sentences.en: But John Ossoff has essentially won this race.
sentences.zh: 但乔恩·奥索夫基本上已经赢得了这场竞选。

sentences.en: I mean, at the moment, he's up by three-tenths of a point,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，目前他领先了0.3个百分点，

sentences.en: 13,000 votes or so.
sentences.zh: 大约13000票左右。

sentences.en: That's a larger lead than Joe Biden's lead was in the final account in Georgia in terms of both percentage points and vote margins.
sentences.zh: 在百分比和票数差距方面，这比乔·拜登在佐治亚州最终计票时的领先优势还要大。

sentences.en: And I mean, all of the remaining vote left is Democratic vote.
sentences.zh: 而且我的意思是，所有剩余的选票都是民主党的选票。

sentences.en: There's 50,000 absentee ballots that are going to break for Ossoff by a two-to-one margin or more.
sentences.zh: 还有50000张缺席选票，奥索夫将以二比一或更高的比例胜出。

sentences.en: There are provisional ballots that are going to break for Ossoff.
sentences.zh: 还有一些临时选票也将投给奥索夫。

sentences.en: It's just there's not a path for David Perdue, even if the networks may not call the race in the immediate future.
sentences.zh: 大卫·珀杜已经没有获胜的途径了，即使媒体可能不会立即宣布结果。

sentences.en: It's not there for the Republicans.
sentences.zh: 共和党人已经没有机会了。

sentences.en: Nate, I think a lot of people listening to you talk the way that you are is going to be among the first times it's dawned on them
sentences.zh: 内特，我想很多听你这样说的人，这可能是他们第一次意识到，

sentences.en: that Democrats are very much on the cusp of retaking control of the Senate.
sentences.zh: 民主党人确实正处于夺回参议院控制权的边缘。

sentences.en: And that has a lot of implications.
sentences.zh: 而这具有很多深远的影响。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, you're right.
sentences.zh: 是的，你是对的。

sentences.en: We can't make the call.
sentences.zh: 我们无法宣布结果。

sentences.en: But the Democrats, for all intents and purposes at this point, will control the Senate.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，民主党人此时将控制参议院。

sentences.en: And the consequences of that for the Biden presidency are enormous.
sentences.zh: 这对拜登总统任期的影响是巨大的。

sentences.en: It will allow them to confirm nominees with considerably greater ease.
sentences.zh: 这将使他们能够以更轻松的方式确认提名人选。

sentences.en: It'll let them pass budget reconciliation packages that let them do all sorts of things with a mere majority of the vote.
sentences.zh: 这将让他们能够通过预算和解方案，从而仅凭多数票就能完成各种事情。

sentences.en: It'll give them control of the committees.
sentences.zh: 这将使他们获得委员会的控制权。

sentences.en: I mean, it will completely transform the first two years of Biden's presidency.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这将彻底改变拜登总统任期的前两年。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app unlocked.
sentences.zh: 解锁《纽约时报》应用程序。

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 每个人都知道你需要订阅《纽约时报》才能访问所有的报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果你可以免费探索《纽约时报》一个月，而无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在应用中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间越过付费墙，看看《纽约时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果您还没有订阅《纽约时报》，请立即下载该应用程序，并获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: So, Nate, turning to the Republican side and to Loeffler and Perdue, there were a lot of questions ahead of these runoffs about the president's message that
sentences.zh: 那么，内特，转到共和党方面，谈谈洛夫勒和珀杜，在这些决选之前，关于总统传达的

sentences.en: the November election had been stolen, his really forceful criticism of election officials in Georgia, whether that was going to depress the Republican vote.
sentences.zh: 11月大选被窃取的信息，以及他对佐治亚州选举官员的严厉批评，是否会压低共和党选票，有很多疑问。

sentences.en: Does that seem to have happened?
sentences.zh: 这种情况似乎发生了吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that's tough to say.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为这很难说。

sentences.en: I mean, the Republican turnout was really healthy by any measure other than the final result.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，除了最终结果之外，共和党的投票率在任何衡量标准下都非常健康。

sentences.en: I mean, the turnout in overwhelmingly Trump precincts was at 88% of the general election.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在特朗普占压倒性优势的选区，投票率达到了大选的88%。

sentences.en: You know, you don't have this sort of stupendous turnout only from one side.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你不会只从一方看到这种惊人的投票率。

sentences.en: You know, clearly the Democratic turnout was superior to the Republican turnout in this election.
sentences.zh: 很明显，这次选举中民主党的投票率优于共和党。

sentences.en: I think that's pretty obvious when you look at the precinct results, at least if you're comparing to the general election and taking that as your baseline.
sentences.zh: 当你查看选区结果时，这很明显，至少如果你将其与大选进行比较并以此为基准的话。

sentences.en: Whether you want to think about that as, you know, the president motivated Democratic Biden voters by, you know, thumbing his nose in the face of their victory
sentences.zh: 无论你是认为总统通过嘲弄他们的胜利而激励了民主党的拜登选民，

sentences.en: and basically, you know, not hearing the message they were trying to send.
sentences.zh: 基本上没有听取他们试图传达的信息，

sentences.en: Or you want to say that he deflated Republican voters by saying their votes wouldn't count.
sentences.zh: 还是你想说他通过声称选票无效而打击了共和党选民的积极性。

sentences.en: And that's very hard for me to untangle.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说很难理清。

sentences.en: And maybe it's some combination of both of them.
sentences.zh: 也许两者兼而有之。

sentences.en: I think a lot of people are wondering if what happened tonight in Georgia starts to tell us something about President Trump and about Trumpism
sentences.zh: 我想很多人都在想，今晚在佐治亚州发生的事情是否开始告诉我们关于特朗普总统和特朗普主义的一些信息，

sentences.en: and whether or not the party can win elections when Donald Trump is not on the ballot.
sentences.zh: 以及当唐纳德·特朗普不在选票上时，该党是否还能赢得选举。

sentences.en: And so what are we learning from the results so far?
sentences.zh: 那么到目前为止，我们从结果中学到了什么？

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, to me, this election was very much dominated by the president.
sentences.zh: 是的，对我来说，这次选举在很大程度上是由总统主导的。

sentences.en: You know, back in November, these two candidates ran ahead of President Trump in Georgia.
sentences.zh: 你知道，早在11月，这两位候选人在佐治亚州的表现都领先于特朗普总统。

sentences.en: Over the last two months, I would argue that they're more tied to the president than ever before.
sentences.zh: 在过去的两个月里，我认为他们与总统的联系比以往任何时候都更加紧密。

sentences.en: And arguably in a way that makes it harder and harder for them to win over the sliver of Biden-Purdue voters that they won in November.
sentences.zh: 可以说，这使得他们越来越难以赢得他们在11月赢得的那一小部分拜登-珀杜选民的支持。

sentences.en: And when you refer to a Biden-Purdue voter, I guess what you mean is, you know, someone who's a moderate Republican in Georgia who might favor Senator Perdue,
sentences.zh: 当你提到拜登-珀杜选民时，我想你的意思是，你知道，佐治亚州那些可能支持珀杜参议员，

sentences.en: who was up for election tonight, and Joe Biden, but might have reservations about Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 也就是今晚参加竞选的人，同时也支持乔·拜登，但可能对唐纳德·特朗普有所保留的温和派共和党人。

sentences.en: Yeah, a rich Republican.
sentences.zh: 是的，富有的共和党人。

sentences.en: And there were a lot of these voters on the north side of Atlanta in the, you know, most affluent areas of North Fulton and DeKalb counties.
sentences.zh: 在亚特兰大北部的北富尔顿县和迪卡尔布县最富裕的地区，有很多这样的选民。

sentences.en: And so, you know, the president has continuously makes it harder for Republicans to distinguish themselves from him.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，总统不断地让共和党人难以将自己与他区分开来。

sentences.en: At the same time, the president does a lot to mobilize and motivate Democrats to come out against him.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，总统做了很多工作来动员和激励民主党人站出来反对他。

sentences.en: And I think that the last two months have done plenty to convince people that they ought to come out and vote
sentences.zh: 我认为过去两个月已经足以说服人们，如果他们是佐治亚州的民主党人，就应该出来投票，

sentences.en: if they're a Democrat in Georgia after, you know, the way the president's acted over the last two months.
sentences.zh: 特别是在总统过去两个月的所作所为之后。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Do you suspect that the results here, and given what you just said, means that the Republican Party is going to want to start untethering itself from Trumpism and from Trump?
sentences.zh: 你是否怀疑这里的结果，以及鉴于你刚才所说的，意味着共和党将想要开始摆脱特朗普主义和特朗普？

sentences.en: Because regardless of the strength of his base, this legendary group of voters that will come out when he asks them to,
sentences.zh: 因为无论他的基本盘有多强大，这群传奇般的选民会在他要求时出来投票，

sentences.en: what happened in Georgia suggests that he is starting to be seen as much as a problem for Republicans as a solution going forward.
sentences.zh: 但佐治亚州发生的事情表明，他开始被视为共和党未来的问题，而不是解决方案。

sentences.en: Yeah, the president has put the Republican Party in a tough spot.
sentences.zh: 是的，总统让共和党陷入了困境。

sentences.en: I mean, the fundamental dynamic that the Republicans face right now, which is the president is just a little bit less popular than they'd like him to be nationwide
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，共和党人目前面临的基本动态是，总统在全国范围内的受欢迎程度比他们希望的要低一点，

sentences.en: and in the critical battleground states and in Georgia, a traditionally Republican state.
sentences.zh: 在关键的摇摆州以及传统的共和党州佐治亚州也是如此。

sentences.en: And as a result, for them to win, they need to win over a few voters, not that many,
sentences.zh: 因此，他们若想获胜，需要争取到少数选民的支持，虽然人数不多，

sentences.en: but a few voters who don't like the president and who maybe used to vote Republican before the president came to dominate American politics.
sentences.zh: 但这些选民不喜欢总统，而且在总统主导美国政治之前，他们可能曾是共和党的支持者。

sentences.en: But he just makes it too hard for them to be able to do that because he's such a dominant force in American life.
sentences.zh: 但他让这些人很难做到这一点，因为他在美国生活中是一个极具统治力的力量。

sentences.en: So in summary, the president looms so large over Republican politics,
sentences.zh: 总而言之，总统在共和党政治中占据了巨大的影响力，

sentences.en: but he's not popular enough to win the crucial moderate votes required to win something like the presidency in Georgia or a Senate race.
sentences.zh: 但他并不受欢迎，不足以赢得在佐治亚州或参议院竞选中获胜所需的关键温和派选票。

sentences.en: And so the party is stuck so long as he remains the most powerful emblem of the Republican brand.
sentences.zh: 因此，只要他仍然是共和党最强大的象征，该党就会陷入困境。

sentences.en: Yep, that's right.
sentences.zh: 没错，确实如此。

sentences.en: Sunit, as you know, in a few hours, Congress is going to convene, and its job will be to certify President-elect Joe Biden's victory in the Electoral College.
sentences.zh: 苏尼特，如你所知，几个小时后国会将召开会议，其任务是认证当选总统乔·拜登在选举人团中的胜利。

sentences.en: Many Republicans intend to object.
sentences.zh: 许多共和党人打算提出异议。

sentences.en: It is expected to be chaotic and polarized and ugly.
sentences.zh: 预计过程会陷入混乱、两极分化和难堪的局面。

sentences.en: And I wonder what Warnock's projected win and Ossoff's lead mean for that process, potentially.
sentences.zh: 我想知道沃诺克的预计获胜和奥索夫的领先优势对这一进程可能意味着什么。

sentences.en: I think it has the potential to change the dynamic a bit.
sentences.zh: 我认为这有可能稍微改变这种动态。

sentences.en: And if you step back for a moment, I mean, the Republicans came out of the November election feeling pretty good in the scheme of having lost a presidential election.
sentences.zh: 如果你退一步看，我的意思是，共和党人在11月大选后，在输掉总统大选的背景下，感觉还不错。

sentences.en: They won a lot of the Senate races they wanted to win.
sentences.zh: 他们赢得了许多他们想要赢得的参议院席位。

sentences.en: The president did better than they expected.
sentences.zh: 总统的表现比他们预期的要好。

sentences.en: And, you know, they didn't have too many reason to think after that that they needed to go and distance themselves from him.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，在那之后他们没有太多理由认为自己需要与他保持距离。

sentences.en: And as a result, many Republicans have been inclined to follow him down an increasingly perilous path toward contesting this presidential election.
sentences.zh: 结果，许多共和党人倾向于跟随他走上一条日益危险的道路，去质疑这次总统大选的结果。

sentences.en: And now Republicans are going to look at a very different set of results.
sentences.zh: 而现在，共和党人将面对一套截然不同的结果。

sentences.en: They're going to look at two Republicans who have loSt.
sentences.zh: 他们将看到两名共和党人落败。

sentences.en: And they will have also, as a result of losing, cost the party control of the Senate.
sentences.zh: 而且，由于这次失败，他们还将使该党失去对参议院的控制权。

sentences.en: Potentially, yes.
sentences.zh: 有可能，是的。

sentences.en: In all likelihood, will cost the party control of the Senate.
sentences.zh: 很有可能，将使该党失去对参议院的控制权。

sentences.en: And I would think that being on the verge of losing control of the Senate would make them at least reconsider the idea that there are no political costs to following the president down this pretty reckless path of challenging legitimate Democratic election results in a half-dozen states.
sentences.zh: 我认为，处于失去参议院控制权的边缘，至少会让他们重新考虑这样一种想法：即跟随总统走上这条在六个州挑战合法民主选举结果的鲁莽道路，是没有政治代价的。

sentences.en: Including, I believe, Georgia?
sentences.zh: 包括佐治亚州吗？

sentences.en: Including Georgia.
sentences.zh: 包括佐治亚州。

sentences.en: Well, Nate, thank you.
sentences.zh: 好的，内特，谢谢你。

sentences.en: Get some reSt.
sentences.zh: 好好休息一下。

sentences.en: We appreciate your time.
sentences.zh: 感谢你的时间。

sentences.en: No problem.
sentences.zh: 没问题。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我。

sentences.en: We were told that we couldn't win this election.
sentences.zh: 有人告诉我们，我们无法赢得这场选举。

sentences.en: But tonight, we prove that with hope, hard work, and the people by our side, anything is possible.
sentences.zh: 但今晚，我们证明了只要有希望、努力工作，并有人民站在我们这边，一切皆有可能。

sentences.en: On Wednesday morning, Rafael Warnock spoke to his supporters, recalling his journey from a public housing project in Savannah to becoming the first Black senator from Georgia.
sentences.zh: 周三上午，拉斐尔·沃诺克向他的支持者发表讲话，回顾了他从萨凡纳公共住房项目到成为佐治亚州首位黑人参议员的历程。

sentences.en: And my mother, who was a teenager growing up in Wake Cross, Georgia, used to pick somebody else's cotton.
sentences.zh: 我的母亲，她十几岁时在佐治亚州的韦克克罗斯长大，过去常常采摘别人的棉花。

sentences.en: But the other day, because this is America,
sentences.zh: 但前几天，因为这就是美国，

sentences.en: the 82-year-old hands that used to pick somebody else's cotton went to the polls and picked her youngest son to be a United States senator.
sentences.zh: 那双曾经采摘别人棉花的82岁的手，走进了投票站，选出了她最小的儿子担任美国参议员。

sentences.en: So I come before you tonight as a man who knows that the improbable journey that led me to this place in this historic moment in America could only happen here.
sentences.zh: 所以我今晚站在你们面前，作为一个深知将我带到这个历史性时刻、这个地方的不可思议的旅程，只有在这里才能发生的人。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的其他消息。

sentences.en: Today, we're going to talk in great detail about the events that happened here in Kenosha on August 23, 2020.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们将详细讨论2020年8月23日发生在基诺沙的事件。

sentences.en: The district attorney in Kenosha, Wisconsin, has declined to bring charges against the white police officer who repeatedly shot a Black man, Jacob Blake, in the back,
sentences.zh: 威斯康星州基诺沙的地区检察官拒绝起诉那名多次向一名黑人男子雅各布·布莱克背部开枪的白人警察，

sentences.en: outside of his apartment in August, a shooting that sparked protests and rioting.
sentences.zh: 那是8月在他公寓外发生的一起枪击事件，引发了抗议和骚乱。

sentences.en: And in this situation, an exhaustive investigation was done.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，已经进行了详尽的调查。

sentences.en: There's more than 40 hours of squad video.
sentences.zh: 有超过40小时的随身摄像机视频。

sentences.en: There's hundreds of pages of electronic information.
sentences.zh: 有数百页的电子信息。

sentences.en: The district attorney, Michael Gravely, said that there was insufficient evidence to bring a charge against the officer who shot Blake after he had resisted arrest,
sentences.zh: 地区检察官迈克尔·格雷夫利表示，没有足够的证据对那名在布莱克拒捕、

sentences.en: avoided a taser, and opened the door to a car where police found a knife.
sentences.zh: 躲避泰瑟枪并打开车门（警方在车内发现了一把刀）后开枪的警察提起诉讼。

sentences.en: The shooting severed Blake's spinal cord, leaving him partially paralyzed and unlikely to ever walk.
sentences.zh: 枪击切断了布莱克的脊髓，导致他部分瘫痪，几乎不可能再行走。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Luke Vanderplug and Daniel Guimet.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由卢克·范德普拉格和丹尼尔·吉梅特制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Lisa Chow and M.J.
sentences.zh: 由丽莎·周和M.J.

sentences.en: Davis-Lynn and engineered by Chris Wood.
sentences.zh: 戴维斯-林恩编辑，克里斯·伍德担任工程制作。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这就是《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine, until this summer, when elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个严密控制的机器运作，直到今年夏天，选举迎来了一批自称改革派的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直处于一场伤痕累累、混乱不堪，有时又令人兴奋的斗争之中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在《地铁》的最新一集中，我和莎拉·凯尼格将讲述人们试图维持影响力却在过程中失去控制的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《地铁》。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 在你获取播客的任何地方收听。

sentences.en: Let's go.
sentences.zh: 我们走吧。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。
